description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects Increased access to informal SMEs and sole proprietors, including women and Silver Customers: informal enterprises in El Salvador account for approximately 21.4% of the country's GDP and around 67.45% of the total employed population. However, because traditional financial institutions typically require formal registration, collateral, and credit history, informal firms have very limited access to credit, relying on informal sources or microfinance institutions and credit cooperatives. The Project will support Banco Agricola in increasing lending to this segment. The Bank will leverage digital banking solutions and innovative lending models that cater specifically to informal SMEs. By integrating these businesses into the formal financial system, Banco Agricola not only supports their long-term sustainability but also contributes to broader economic development.
Stakeholder effects Increased access to finance for SMEs, including women SMEs (WSMEs): IFC anticipates that the Project will improve access to finance for SMEs in El Salvador. Based on the World Banks 2023 Enterprise Survey for El Salvador, 15.7% of all firms and 19.5% of small firms consider access to finance as a major or severe obstacle. WSMEs have larger financing gaps than their male-owned peers. They tend to be smaller, less likely to have a savings account, and face a higher cost of credit. Banco Agricola will enhance its new SME and digital strategies and digitizing its SME product lines with the aim of increasing the Banks lending to the SME segment.
At the market level, IFC anticipates that the Project will enhance competitiveness in El Salvadors financial market by addressing inclusion disparities, with a particular focus on empowering SMEs, informal SMEs, and sole proprietors. Banco Agrícola has set an ambitious goal to expand its offerings for informal SMEs and sole proprietors, with a strong emphasis on supporting women and silver economy entrepreneurs.

The proposed investment consists of a US$200 million financing package to Banco Agricola S.A. in El Salvador, composed of: 1) an up to US$115 million senior unsecured A loan for IFC's own account (IFC A Loan), to be committed in one single tranche; and 2) an up to US$85 million senior unsecured B Loan (B Loan), split into two tranches: (i) tranche 1: up to US$35 million, to be committed at the moment of the IFC A Loan commitment; and (ii) tranche 2: up to US$50 million, to be committed within up to 18 months after Tranche 1.
